title: Test Your Understanding: Design a Chat System
description: WebSockets, ordering, presence, and offline sync.

questions.question: Per-conversation server_seq primarily provides:

options.text: Global ordering across all users in the system
Monotonic ordering of messages within one conversation

questions.explanation: Each conversation has its own sequence — clients sync with after_seq cursor; cross-chat order rarely matters.

questions.question: client_msg_id exists mainly to:

options.text: Deduplicate retries from the sender's mobile client

questions.explanation: Unique (conversation_id, client_msg_id) makes resends idempotent — one bubble per user intent.

questions.question: WebSocket gateways are typically sharded by:

options.text: user_id so inbound messages route to the correct connection
Random round robin only with no registry

questions.explanation: Stateful connections need routing — hash user_id to gateway instance or connection registry lookup.

questions.question: Typing indicators are best stored in:
questions.explanation: High churn, no durability need — ephemeral channel avoids DB write storms.

questions.question: Sharding messages by conversation_id helps because:

options.text: All messages in a chat live on one shard — ordering stays local
It eliminates need for sequence numbers

questions.explanation: Conversation-local shard keeps append and range queries for history on one partition.

questions.question: When a recipient is offline, delivery often falls back to:

options.text: Push notification plus sync API on next app open

questions.explanation: Persist message, notify via push, client catches up with ?after_seq= on reconnect.

questions.question: Under network partition, many chat products favor accepting the send and delivering eventually over failing the send.
questions.explanation: Availability bias — users expect messages to send; sync heals ordering gaps when partition heals.

questions.question: Group chat at scale requires: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Fan-out delivery to each member's gateway or push path
One WebSocket write to a magic broadcast address with no infra
Storing typing events in the primary messages table

questions.explanation: N-1 deliveries per message; batch by connection server. Typing stays ephemeral.
